newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended flat in Friday's listless trade, but a swathe of overnight foreign assets swaps boostd volumes as Gencor closed with 4.1 million shares traded on the counter, dealers said.

Gencor ended down 80 cents at 19.75 rand following a large corporate finance deal on the stock involving some 3.2 million shares valued at around 67 million rand earlier, dealers said. "The market is off but as you know we've seen big volumes because of overnight trades here," one dealer said.
He added that some reluctance by market players to take positions ahead of the June futures close-out next week hurt the industrials which were also weighed down by profit taking.
"I still think the guys are very cautious ahead of the long-weekend and of the futures-close out. They are not taking any positions," the dealer added.
Industrials ended down 19.7 points at 8,482.4, golds were off 19.1 points at 1,129.0 and the all-share index closed down 21.2 points at 7,271.5.
Dealers said bullion's hold below the pshycologically-important $350 an ounce level continued to cripple golds.
"Gold are still doing nothing because of the gold price," one dealer said.
Gold mining firm, Goldfields was last down 275 cents at 105.00 rand, Western Areas off 190 cents at 38.60 rand and Vaal Reefs down 250 cents to 262.50 rand.

Dealers said while precious metal stocks were in gloom, the finance and banking sectors continued to tread on positive ground with continuing hopes that Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals might cut interest rates later this year.
The financial index hit another fresh high on Friday when it added 21.9 points to 9,805.9.

"I think the important thing on the financial sector now is the clarity about the decline of interest rates," Tracy Ledger, an equities trader at stockbroking firm BoE Natwest Securities, told Reuters.
"The banking shares are powering ahead and are looking very nice because there is a belief that a cut in interest rate is going to open up some profit margins," she added.
First National Bank gained 125 cents to a fresh year high of 39.25 rand and Nedcor added 150 cents to a record 96.00 rand.
Dealers said despite a lethargic trade session volumes ended strong with around 860 million rand worth of shares traded by close compared to 901 million rand worth of shares on Thursday.
In the broader market the declines led advances by 220 to 152, while 31 shares hit new highs and 27 dropped to new lows.
Johannesburg Stock Exchange officials said an all time weekly high of 52,138 deals or trades had been reached on Friday.
The previous high of 50,197 was recorded in the week ended 16 May, they added.

Dealers said they expected some volatility in next weeks' four-day trade as market players square-up for positions amid the June futures close-out then. The bourse will be closed on Monday, June 16, for Youth Day holiday.
As in the cash market, the South African share futures ignored Wall Street's record overnight climb and also took a knock from a weaker local bond market.
Dealers said by Friday's close there had been little change as worries over the futures close-out remained and some niggling concerns over the relaxation of foreign exchange controls on July 1.
"The market has closed weak. There are still concerns about foreign exchange controls and nervousness on the futures close-out next week," one futures trader said.
"I think no one is going to get involved unless we get these things out of the way," he added.
The June all-share contract was last at 6,510/25 from 6,572 settlement, the June gold contract at 787/92 from 803 settlement and the June industrial contract at 8,071/82 from 8,159 settlement.
-- Ellis Mnyandu, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
